q: What does Lightwave Logic actually make?
a: Electro-optic (EO) polymers: engineered plastic-like materials, sold under the Perkinamine® name, that change how light travels when a voltage is applied. Put on a silicon photonics chip, they form modulators, the part of an optical transceiver that turns electrical data into pulses of light. The business model is material supply plus licensing to chip and transceiver makers.

The company describes a four-stage design-win cycle: (1) technology selection, (2) product design, (3) prototype to final product, (4) production ramp. Five Fortune Global 500 programs were reported in Stage 3 at the Q2 2026 call. None has been disclosed in Stage 4.

q: How long will the cash last?

q: Why do short sellers bet against it?
a: The usual arguments are minimal revenue after decades of development, dilution, insider selling, competition from other materials, and a valuation ahead of fundamentals. Each one is answered on the bull vs. bear page.
